program_name: Mathematical Engineering — this is the official ENGLISH degree title, and the programme is a STANDALONE degree, not a curriculum inside an Italian-taught degree (this confirms the research brief's "type: standalone"). The official Italian title is "Ingegneria Matematica". The binding Didactic Regulations state both in a single table: "Name of the Course in Italian: Ingegneria Matematica | Name of the Course in English: Mathematical Engineering | Class: LM-44 Mathematical-Physics modelling for Engineering | Teaching language: English | Web site of the Course: http://www.mathematical-engineering.unina.it". The Italian diploma will therefore read "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Matematica"; the long form used in official English prose is "Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Mathematical Engineering" / "Master Degree Program in Mathematical Engineering". The ministerial RAD/ordinamento sheet on unina.it records the Italian name as "Ingegneria Matematica (riformulazione di Ingegneria Matematica)" and the English name as "Mathematical Engineering", i.e. the course now offered is a re-formulation of the degree originally designed after consultations with the Unione degli Industriali della Provincia di Napoli (September 2015) and CIRA - Centro Italiano Ricerche Aerospaziali (October 2015) and proposed for activation in a.a. 2016/2017. INTERNAL UNIVERSITY COURSE CODE: D71 — the programme's own "General Information" page gives "Web Corsi di Studio: https://www.corsi.unina.it/D71/home". A second code, D22, also resolves to a "MATHEMATICAL ENGINEERING" record on corsi.unina.it and appears to be the legacy pre-reformulation code (see uncertainty_notes). ADMINISTERING DEPARTMENT: Dipartimento di Matematica e Applicazioni "Renato Caccioppoli" (Department of Mathematics and Applications). SCHOOL/FACULTY: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School, PBSS/SPSB). Teaching area recorded centrally: "Scienze MM.FF.NN.". Duration 2 years, 120 CFU. TWO INTERNAL CURRICULA: Curriculum A (more oriented towards information engineering applications) and Curriculum B (more oriented towards industrial and civil engineering applications). These are specialisation tracks inside the SAME English-taught degree; they are not separate degree programmes and do not change the diploma title. Teaching staff is drawn from the Department of Mathematics and from several Engineering Departments. DEGREE PROGRAMME DIRECTOR / COORDINATOR: Prof.ssa Lina Mallozzi (lina.mallozzi@unina.it, tel. 081 7682476) — stated both on the orientation portal ("Lina Mallozzi — Degree Programme Director") and on the programme's own "Programme Administration" page ("Coordinator: Lina Mallozzi"). Contact person for International Students: Prof. Marco Lapegna (lapegna@unina.it, tel. 081 675623). Contact person for student orientation: Prof. Salvatore Cuomo (salvatore.cuomo@unina.it). Programme mailbox: infomathematical-eng@unina.it; department phone +39 081 7682476. NOTE A COORDINATOR CONFLICT: the central unina.it course record still names "Prof.ssa Anna MERCALDO" as Coordinatore — see uncertainty_notes. Internal double-degree options ("Doppie Lauree Magistrali Interne") exist with the MSc in Mathematics and with MSc programmes in Engineering, plus an International Double Degree Master Program. level: master (Italian "Laurea Magistrale", second-cycle degree, 2 years, 120 CFU). The central unina.it course record states "Tipo di corso: Magistrale", "Durata: 2 anni", "Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 1° livello". The orientation portal fact sheet is headed "Master's Degree — Mathematical Engineering" with "Degree required: Laurea I Livello". The programme's own General Information page states "Degree level: Laurea Magistrale [MSc]; Programme duration: 2 years; Teaching language: English". This confirms the research brief's "level: master". CREDIT STRUCTURE (Art. 9 of the Didactic Regulations, unchanged in the 2026/2027 study plan): "The student must acquire 120 CFU, attributable to the following Types of Training Activities (TAF): B) characterising, 75; C) related or complementary, 12; D) at the student's choice, 12; E) for the final exam, 18; F) further training activities, 3." Each CFU = 25 hours of total student workload. The degree is awarded after passing no more than 12 examinations INCLUDING the final exam. FIRST YEAR (identical core for both curricula): Real and Functional Analysis (9 CFU, MATH-03/A, sem. 1), Mathematical Physics Models (9 CFU, MATH-04/A, sem. 1), Numerical Methods (9 CFU, MATH-05/A, sem. 2), Thermodynamics and Transport Phenomena (9 CFU, IMAT-01/A, sem. 2), Nonlinear Systems (9 CFU, IINF-04/A, sem. 2), plus one 6-CFU option from GROUP 1 and one 12-CFU two-module option from GROUP 3. SECOND YEAR: Computational Fluid Dynamics (9 CFU, IIND-01/F, sem. 1) and Electrodynamics of Continuous Media (9 CFU, IIET-01/A, sem. 2) are mandatory in BOTH curricula, plus one 6-CFU option from GROUP 2, 12 CFU of autonomously chosen topics (TAF D), 3 CFU "Other" (TAF F) and the 18-CFU final test (TAF E). The 3 CFU of "Further Activities" are earned by attending seminars — the programme runs its own series, "Colloquia in Mathematical Engineering", and attendance at credit-bearing seminar activities is compulsory. FINAL EXAM: "Every student will choose the subject of the thesis according to the suggestions of a supervisor... All students must defend their master's thesis. Such a defense consists of an oral presentation and answering questions from a Committee" — 20 minutes of presentation plus 5 minutes of questions. Graduates may continue directly into PhD programmes. NO INTERNAL PROPEDEUTICITÀ (course prerequisite chain) is listed in the 2026/2027 study plan.
teaching_language: English — the programme is declared 100% English-taught by every official unina.it source, and unusually for Federico II this is verifiable course-by-course. EVIDENCE: (1) the orientation portal fact-sheet header records "Language ENG" (a single value, not the ITA/ENG pairing used for bilingual courses in the same catalogue); (2) the binding Didactic Regulations record "Teaching language: English" in the SUA-CdS general information table; (3) Annex 2 of the Didactic Regulations lists EVERY ONE of the 39 course sheets with the teaching language "English" — including the engineering-hosted courses (Computational Fluid Dynamics, Electrodynamics of Continuous Media, Theory of Elasticity, Heat Transfer, Optoelectronics, Electromagnetic Fields, Information Theory, Mechanical Vibrations, Environment Fluid Dynamics and Hydraulics, Nonlinear Dynamics and Control) and the physics/chemistry/statistics modules in Group 3; (4) the programme's own General Information page states "Teaching language: English"; (5) the ministerial RAD sheet records "Lingua in cui si tiene il corso: inglese" and the University's own evaluation unit noted that the course "sarà tenuto in lingua inglese" and fits the University's internationalisation policy. BLENDED / MIXED DELIVERY (this is a real feature of this degree, not a caveat about language): the Didactic Regulations record the teaching method as "b. Course of Studies in mixed teaching mode", and the orientation portal explains "Some courses in the first semester of the first year are delivered partially in a blended format, with online components provided via the Federica Web Learning platform (https://www.federica.eu/). At the beginning of the semester, students will attend an online orientation meeting where they will receive detailed instructions on the course structure and how to follow the online components." The 2026/2027 study plan marks the affected courses "Frontal lesson/MOOC" — Real and Functional Analysis, Mathematical Physics Models, Mathematical Methods for Engineering, Calculus of Variations, Differential Geometry, Stochastic Processes and Mechanical Vibrations. NOTE A MINOR SOURCE CONFLICT: the older ministerial RAD sheet records "Modalità di svolgimento: convenzionale" (conventional delivery), which the current Didactic Regulations supersede with "mixed teaching mode". NO ITALIAN IS REQUIRED AT ANY POINT — and this is a material difference from some other Federico II English-taught degrees. The 3-CFU "Further training activities" (TAF F) slot is earned through SEMINAR attendance ("Mathematical Engineering students can attend seminars to complete 3 CFU as 'Further Activities'. A series of seminars is organized by the MS program, Colloquia in Mathematical Engineering"), NOT through an Italian-language certificate. Italian courses are offered to international students by the University Language Centre (CLA) on a free, optional, self-study basis through the ICoN Consortium at CEFR levels A1-C1 ("Participation in the courses is free of charge and the licence is valid for one year"). [uncertain] THE ONE RESIDUAL RISK IS THE 12-CFU FREE-CHOICE SLOT (TAF D, "Autonomously chosen topics", second year): Art. 9 of the Didactic Regulations states "the student is free to choose among all the Courses offered by the University, provided that they are consistent with the training project. This consistency is assessed by the Didactic Coordination Commission." Because that slot draws on the University's entire catalogue — most of which is Italian-taught — a student who cannot follow Italian must deliberately pick English-delivered courses for those 12 CFU. All MANDATORY and all curricular OPTION courses (Groups 1, 2 and 3) are confirmed English; only the free-choice slot is unconstrained.

admission_type: OPEN ACCESS ("accesso libero") — NO numerus clausus, NO seat cap, NO ranked competitive selection, NO admission test. The orientation portal fact-sheet header records "Admission: Libero" and "Degree required: Laurea I Livello". The programme does NOT appear anywhere in the University's index of "Corsi a numero programmato" for a.y. 2026/2027 (the only two-year master's degrees with a bando there are Precision Livestock Farming, Professioni sanitarie, Psicologia Clinica, Scienze Enologiche and Scienze della Nutrizione Umana — all restricted-access). BUT "OPEN ACCESS" HERE DOES NOT MEAN "AUTOMATIC": admission is gated by a MANDATORY two-part check that the Didactic Regulations make explicit. Art. 5: "Admission to the master's degree course in Mathematical Engineering will be arranged by the Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico after checking: a) the requirement of knowledge of the English language, corresponding to a level of knowledge not lower than level B2, possibly attested by suitable certification; b) the adequacy of the student's personal preparation, for the purposes of admission to the Master's Degree Course, according to the provisions of the art. 6 comma 2 of D.M. 16 marzo 2007, with procedures common to the Master's Degree Courses in Engineering governed by the device of the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base." The Italian text is blunter: "La verifica della personale preparazione è obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari" (the personal-preparation check is compulsory in every case, and only students who already hold the curricular requirements may take it). The Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base confirms the framework at School level: "L'ammissione ai Corsi di Laurea Magistrale non a ciclo unico prevede, ai sensi del DM 270/04, la verifica del possesso dei requisiti curriculari nonché la verifica della personale preparazione dello studente." THREE PRACTICAL ROUTES: (1) ITALIAN APPLICANTS — "Italian students can enroll at www.segrepass.unina.it" (programme's own 2026/27 admission rules); the Segreteria checks the curricular requirements and communicates the outcome, and an enrolment made without the requirements is annulled. (2) EU APPLICANTS / APPLICANTS RESIDENT IN THE EU WITH A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION — no competitive application; per international.unina.it they "have unrestricted access to university courses if you hold a foreign qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification. In this case you have to send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements." (3) NON-EU APPLICANTS RESIDING ABROAD — compulsory pre-enrolment on the UNIVERSITALY portal, followed by evaluation by the University International Office AND the Mathematical Engineering Program Committee, probable interview, and issue of a pre-acceptance letter. Note the programme's distinctive instruction on sequencing: "in order to apply for admission... you must submit your application on the Universitaly portal www.universitaly.it. In this step the pre-acceptance letter is not necessary." — i.e. unlike several other Federico II degrees, this programme wants you to apply on Universitaly FIRST and lets the pre-acceptance letter be generated afterwards. Because the course is accesso libero, no bando di ammissione is published for it; the functional equivalent is the programme's one-page "GENERAL ADMISSION RULES" PDF for the year (see official_call_url).
academic_requirements:
A first-cycle degree (Laurea triennale / Bachelor) in engineering, mathematics or building sciences, PLUS specific minimum credits in mathematics, physics and computing, PLUS English at B2. TWO PARALLEL FORMULATIONS EXIST — one for Italian-system qualifications and one for foreign qualifications.

(A) ITALIAN-SYSTEM ROUTE — DEGREE CLASS LIST (Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations, identical in the Italian 2023/24 and English 2025/26 versions and in the ministerial RAD sheet): "Access to the master's degree course in Mathematical Engineering will be allowed to students holding a Degree in the Classes L-7 Civil and Environmental Engineering, L-8 Information Engineering, L-9 Industrial Engineering, L-23 Building Sciences and Techniques, L-35 Mathematical Sciences" — the Italian original adds "ovvero titoli equipollenti" (or equivalent qualifications).

(B) MINIMUM CREDIT THRESHOLDS — this is the hard, quantified requirement, and it appears ONLY in the newer (2025/26) English Didactic Regulations, not in the 2023/24 Italian text: "In particular, the student must have acquired a minimum of 24 CFU in mathematics SSD, of which 6 in MATH-02/B and 18 in MATH-03/A, a minimum of 12 CFU in physics SSD PHYS-01/A and a minimum of 6 CFU in INFO-01/A or IINF-05/A." These are the post-2023 Italian scientific-disciplinary sector codes. Their meaning can be read off the programme's own 2026/2027 study plan, which tags Real and Functional Analysis / Calculus of Variations / Partial Differential Equations / Mathematical Methods for Engineering as MATH-03/A (mathematical analysis), Differential Geometry and Geometric Structures and Topology as MATH-02/B (geometry), and Algorithms and Parallel Computing / Deep Learning / Computational Complexity as INFO-01/A (computer science). PHYS-01/A conventionally denotes experimental physics and IINF-05/A information-processing systems, but those two mappings are inferred from standard MUR nomenclature rather than from a unina.it page. IN PLAIN TERMS: expect to need roughly 18 CFU of mathematical analysis, 6 CFU of geometry/algebra, 12 CFU of physics and 6 CFU of computer science in your bachelor transcript.

(C) FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION ROUTE (programme's "GENERAL ADMISSION RULES a.y. 26/27"): "Applicants must have: a Bachelor's degree corresponding to the Italian qualification Laurea, awarded by an accredited foreign university and giving access to second-cycle courses; recommended background are in Mathematics or Engineering with a solid training in the core disciplines: mathematical analysis, algebra and geometry, physics, numerical analysis; a B2 English certification...; a letter of recommendation from a teacher expressly addressed to Mathematical Engineering course (subject to verification)." NOTE THE LETTER OF RECOMMENDATION — it is a genuine programme-specific admission requirement, unusual among Federico II degrees, and it must be addressed to this course by name.

(D) THE ORIENTATION PORTAL USES SOFTER, MORE HOLISTIC WORDING: "Students applying for the Master's Programme in Mathematical Engineering are generally expected to hold a Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Engineering, Physics, or a closely related discipline. Each application will be assessed holistically. Applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency at a B2 level. International students holding an Italian university degree may be admitted to the graduate programme under the same conditions as Italian students." Note that this version admits PHYSICS graduates, whereas the strict Art. 4 class list (L-7/L-8/L-9/L-23/L-35) does not include the physics class L-30 except through "titoli equipollenti".

[uncertain] THE THREE FORMULATIONS ARE NOT IDENTICAL AND THE UNIVERSITY HAS NOT RECONCILED THEM: the degree-class list is closed and engineering/maths-only; the credit thresholds are precise but appear only in the 2025/26 regulations; the foreign-applicant rules speak of a "recommended background" rather than a hard list; and the orientation portal promises holistic assessment and names Physics. A physics or applied-mathematics graduate is very likely admissible in practice via the "equivalent qualifications" clause and the holistic evaluation, but should confirm with infomathematical-eng@unina.it before relying on it. Note also that no MINIMUM GRADE is published anywhere for this programme — unlike the Data Science LM at the same university, Mathematical Engineering sets no GPA threshold on unina.it.

IF YOU DO NOT MEET THE REQUIREMENTS: enrolment is refused, not conditioned. The University FAQ for open-access two-year master's degrees states "Posso immatricolarmi se non possiedo i requisiti di accesso? No. Prima di immatricolarsi è necessario acquisire i requisiti di accesso richiesti", that missing requirements are acquired by enrolling in single course units ("Corsi Singoli"), and that "Verificata la mancanza dei requisiti di accesso, la Segreteria Studenti avvierà il procedimento di annullamento dell'immatricolazione." The Segreteria communicates the outcome of the CV evaluation by PEC, telephone, ordinary e-mail or post. CREDIT RECOGNITION: CFU earned as single courses may be recognised up to a limit of 36 CFU, on the student's request and subject to approval. LATE-ENROLMENT CONDITION: under the University's 2026/27 enrolment guide, a Teaching Coordination Committee may require anyone enrolling in a two-year master's after 31 December 2026 to first acquire between 6 and 12 CFU through single course units.
entry_exam_or_test:
NO WRITTEN ADMISSION TEST, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO PORTFOLIO — but there IS a compulsory evaluation, and for non-EU applicants a PROBABLE INTERVIEW. This is a materially stricter picture than the bare "Admission: Libero" label suggests.

NO TOLC: the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base runs the TOLC only for BACHELOR's degrees — "la Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base... effettua un test di orientamento non selettivo ma obbligatorio per tutti gli immatricolandi ai Corsi di Laurea dei Collegi di Ingegneria e di Scienze" — and expressly applies a different regime to master's degrees: "L'ammissione ai Corsi di Laurea Magistrale non a ciclo unico prevede, ai sensi del DM 270/04, la verifica del possesso dei requisiti curriculari nonché la verifica della personale preparazione dello studente." No TOLC, TOLC-I or TOLC-B applies to Mathematical Engineering.

WHAT REPLACES A TEST — THE "VERIFICA DELLA PERSONALE PREPARAZIONE": Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations makes it compulsory in every case ("La verifica della personale preparazione è obbligatoria in ogni caso"), carried out by the Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico, checking (a) English at B2 or above and (b) "the adequacy of the student's personal preparation... according to the provisions of the art. 6 comma 2 of D.M. 16 marzo 2007, with procedures common to the Master's Degree Courses in Engineering governed by the device of the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base of the University of Naples Federico II."

[uncertain] THE INTERVIEW: the programme's own "GENERAL ADMISSION RULES a.y. 26/27" states, of non-EU applicants who have applied on Universitaly, "Once the students apply on Universitaly portal, the documents will be verified by the University International Office and by the Program Committee members in order to produce the pre-acceptance letter in case of eligibility. Applicants will probably contacted for an interview with Program Committee members of the Mathematical Engineering Course to certify that the educational background is adequate according the requirements of the Master Program (Art. 4 - Didactical Regulations)." The word is "probably" (the sentence is also grammatically incomplete in the original — "will probably contacted"), so the interview is presented as likely but not guaranteed, and no format, length, language, syllabus or scoring scheme is published. Treat it as: prepare for an academic interview in English on your mathematics/engineering background, but do not expect published rules. No equivalent interview is announced for Italian or EU applicants, for whom the check is documentary.

THE ENGLISH GATE IS ENFORCED AFTER ENROLMENT, NOT BY EXAM AT ADMISSION: "Students are allowed to the academic career (specifically exams) only after that the B2 English certification has been verified by the University Language Centre (CLA) presenting one of the above mentioned certifications, otherwise students have to acquire the B2 English level by passing an exam taken at CLA." So a student can enrol without an accepted certificate but cannot sit any examination until CLA has either validated a certificate or the student has passed CLA's own B2 English exam. This is the only examination in the whole admission pipeline, and it is a language exam, not a subject test.

NO ITALIAN LANGUAGE TEST applies: the degree is English-taught, so the University's B2 Italian requirement is waived (see language_requirements).

ATTENDANCE, once admitted, is "strongly recommended but not compulsory" for lectures, except that "Attendance at seminar activities that award training credits is compulsory" (the 3-CFU TAF F slot).
seats_total: NO SEAT CAP — no total number of places is set or published for this programme, because it is accesso libero. The orientation portal fact sheet records "Admission: Libero"; the programme appears nowhere in the University's "Corsi a numero programmato" index for a.y. 2026/2027; the Didactic Regulations contain no numero-programmato provision (Art. 5 merely notes that nationally programmed access is regulated by L. 264/1999 "except in cases subject to different provisions of law", which do not apply here); and the ministerial RAD sheet publishes no "utenza sostenibile" figure or seat number. [uncertain] ONLY IN THE SENSE THAT A NULL IS BEING REPORTED RATHER THAN A NUMBER: no unina.it page states a figure, and none states in so many words that the number is unlimited. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR APPLICANTS: there is no cut-off to beat and no ranking list — the gates are the curricular requirements, the personal-preparation check, the B2 English certificate and (for non-EU applicants) the visa/pre-enrolment pipeline, not competition for places. For comparison, where Federico II does cap a two-year master's it says so numerically in a published bando; no such document exists for Mathematical Engineering.
non_eu_reserved_seats: NONE PUBLISHED — because the course has no seat cap, no reserved sub-quota for non-EU applicants residing abroad appears on any unina.it page for this programme. [uncertain] WITH ONE STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: Italian universities must still declare an annual contingent of places for non-EU visa students on the ministerial UNIVERSITALY portal even for open-access courses, and that per-course figure is published on universitaly.it rather than on unina.it, so it could not be verified within the unina.it-only source restriction imposed by this research task. What unina.it does publish is a soft capacity constraint expressed as a DATE rather than a number: after the 15 June 2026 pre-enrolment deadline, "pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only" — meaning an open-access programme such as Mathematical Engineering simply stops accepting new non-EU pre-enrolments on that date and does not reopen. Applicants should check the Mathematical Engineering entry on universitaly.it for the intake year they are targeting, or write to infomathematical-eng@unina.it and to the University international office.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH AT B2 OR ABOVE — a hard admission requirement, with a NAMED and CLOSED list of accepted certificate providers and a two-year recency rule that is unusually strict for Federico II. ITALIAN IS NOT REQUIRED AT ANY STAGE, including graduation.

THE REQUIREMENT. Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations: "Knowledge of the English language corresponding to at least B2 level will also be required." Art. 5 adds that the CCD verifies "the requirement of knowledge of the English language, corresponding to a level of knowledge not lower than level B2, possibly attested by suitable certification". The orientation portal states flatly "Applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency at a B2 level."

THE ACCEPTED CERTIFICATES (programme's "GENERAL ADMISSION RULES a.y. 26/27", verbatim): "a B2 English certification is also required as IELTS, PEARSON, TOEFL, UNIVERSITY of CAMBRIDGE ESOL, TRINITY, LCCIEB, CITY&GUILDS certifications obtained in the last two years". TWO CRITICAL DETAILS: (i) the list is specific — IELTS, Pearson, TOEFL, Cambridge English (ESOL), Trinity, LCCIEB (London Chamber of Commerce and Industry Examinations Board) and City & Guilds; (ii) the certificate must have been OBTAINED IN THE LAST TWO YEARS, so an older certificate will not be accepted even if the awarding body never expires it. Plan your test date accordingly.

[uncertain] A TENSION BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL WORDINGS: the Didactic Regulations say the B2 level is "possibly attested by suitable certification" ("eventualmente attestato da idonea certificazione") — permissive language that would allow the CCD to accept other evidence — whereas the programme's annual admission rules present the named certificate list as a flat requirement for non-EU applicants. The safe reading is that the named list governs in practice. Neither source states whether an English-medium bachelor's degree can substitute for a certificate, and no unina.it page for this programme confirms or denies that, so applicants relying on an English-taught degree instead of a test should confirm with infomathematical-eng@unina.it.

ENFORCEMENT IS POST-ENROLMENT AND HAS TEETH: "Students are allowed to the academic career (specifically exams) only after that the B2 English certification has been verified by the University Language Centre (CLA) presenting one of the above mentioned certifications, otherwise students have to acquire the B2 English level by passing an exam taken at CLA." So the CLA — not the department — validates the certificate, and a student without an accepted one must pass CLA's own B2 English examination before being allowed to sit any subject examination. The CLA (https://www.cla.unina.it/) runs B1/B2 English workshops in the departments and administers Cambridge English, IELTS, TOEFL/TOEIC and PTE Academic.

ITALIAN: NOT REQUIRED — NOT FOR ADMISSION, NOT FOR THE VISA, AND NOT FOR GRADUATION. Because Mathematical Engineering is English-taught, the University-wide rule applies: "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required." (Note the drafting gap flagged in uncertainty_notes: that exemption sentence enumerates "three-year, five-year or single-cycle" without repeating "magistral degree course", although the parallel Italian-taught clause does name master's degrees; the intent is plainly that English-taught two-year master's degrees are exempt.) Unlike Federico II's Data Science LM, this programme attaches NO Italian-language condition to its "Further training activities" credits — the 3 CFU are earned by seminar attendance. Italian is therefore purely optional here: the CLA offers international students free self-study online Italian courses through the ICoN Consortium at CEFR A1, A2, B1, B2 and C1, "Participation in the courses is free of charge and the licence is valid for one year", enrolled via a form with a UNINA institutional e-mail (corsi.cla@unina.it, https://www.cla.unina.it/corsidilinguaitalianaicon).

VISA-SIDE NOTE: international.unina.it advises that "an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation", so the same B2 certificate should be uploaded to Universitaly.

OUTPUT LANGUAGE: the final examination is an oral defence of the master's thesis before a Committee (20 minutes' presentation plus 5 minutes of questions); no unina.it page for this programme states an explicit language rule for the thesis text, though the degree being wholly English-taught implies English.

[uncertain] A DATE CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL UNINA SOURCES. The programme's orientation-portal page says "Enrollment to Mathematical Engineering is usually possible from 16 July until 31 October", and the orientation portal's own 2026/27 enrolment announcement (published 14 July 2026) says "Anche quest'anno è possibile procedere all'immatricolazione a partire dal 16 luglio e fino al 31 ottobre 2026". (1) THE PROGRAMME DELETED ITS OWN DEADLINE. The programme's "GENERAL ADMISSION RULES a.y. 25/26" contained an explicit, EARLIER programme-level cut-off: "you must submit your application on the Universitaly portal www.universitaly.it BEFORE 31 MAY 2025". Its "Deadlines" page says 31 January 2027, but its "Matriculation (final enrolment)" page says "Students who obtained visa are required to matriculate by 31 January 2026" — a year earlier, which is impossible given the 30 November 2026 visa deadline. 31 JANUARY 2027 is the correct figure; the 2026 reading is an uncorrected carry-over.

[uncertain] THERE IS NO SINGLE CONSOLIDATED CHECKLIST ON THE PROGRAMME SITE — the list below is assembled from the programme's own one-page admission rules plus the University-level booklet, admission regulation and open-access master's FAQ, so the Segreteria or the Program Committee could request an additional item.

(1) PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ITEMS (from "Mathematical Engineering Master Program a.y. 26/27: GENERAL ADMISSION RULES"), for non-EU applicants:
— evidence of "a Bachelor's degree corresponding to the Italian qualification Laurea, awarded by an accredited foreign university and giving access to second-cycle courses";
— A B2 ENGLISH CERTIFICATE from IELTS, PEARSON, TOEFL, University of Cambridge ESOL, TRINITY, LCCIEB or CITY&GUILDS, "obtained in the last two years";
— A LETTER OF RECOMMENDATION FROM A TEACHER "expressly addressed to Mathematical Engineering course (subject to verification)" — this is a genuine programme-specific requirement and is not part of the generic Federico II document set;
— transcript evidence sufficient for the Program Committee to check Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations (the 24 CFU mathematics / 12 CFU physics / 6 CFU computing thresholds), i.e. a transcript showing credits and subject areas.

(2) FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT ON UNIVERSITALY (uploaded as PDF), Master's-degree track, per the University's 2026/2027 booklet: "Transcript of Records (ToR); Final degree certificate; Detailed course descriptions; Additional documents e.g. language certificates, motivation letter, reference letters; Pre-acceptance letter from the Programme Coordinator; DoV or CIMEA both Statement of comparability and verification." Plus, in the application itself, personal data exactly as on the passport and the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested.

(3) QUALIFICATION-RECOGNITION DOCUMENTS (mandatory at enrolment): a DECLARATION OF VALUE (DoV) issued by an Italian Embassy/Consulate — or, as an alternative, the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND Statement of Verification JOINTLY (https://cimea-diplome.it/). If the qualification comes from a European Higher Education Area / Bologna Process country, submit a DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT accompanied by a CIMEA Statement of Verification. Holders of qualifications from Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory countries may use CIMEA's ARDI platform for a Statement of Correspondence plus a Statement of Verification. "At the enrolment stage, the above-mentioned documents are mandatory and must accompany the submitted/declared academic qualifications."

(4) FOR THE ITALIAN EMBASSY / VISA: the validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; language certificates; health insurance; and proof of means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year (plus funds for repatriation, suitable accommodation and adequate insurance cover). NOTE: the same international.unina.it page also carries a much lower figure, EUR 6,079.45 per year / EUR 467.95 per month, but that one is explicitly labelled "minimum required for 2022" and applies to RESIDENCE-PERMIT RENEWAL, not to the entry visa; it has not been refreshed for 2026/27.

(5) FOR ENROLMENT (MATRICULATION) AT THE STUDENT OFFICE, international students: copy of passport; application form; 1 passport photo; Italian tax code (codice fiscale — "mandatory for enrolment... You may start the process without it, but you must obtain it to complete enrolment", obtainable from Agenzia delle Entrate or an Italian embassy); residence permit or proof of having applied for it; Declaration of Value or ENIC-NARIC/CIMEA certificate. Foreign-citizenship students must enrol IN PERSON at the counter of the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Scienze MM.FF.NN. and cannot use the online procedure.

(6) FOR EU / EU-RESIDENT APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION, sent to the course Coordinator for the eligibility check: "any documentation that the University deems necessary for the evaluation of the foreign qualification: eventual translations; legalisations; Diploma Supplement; certificates of examinations; certificates from the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA); any declarations of value issued by the competent diplomatic representations."

(7) FOR ITALIAN-QUALIFICATION APPLICANTS ENROLLING VIA SEGREPASS (www.segrepass.unina.it): the printed plico from the matriculation procedure, a passport-size photo, a photocopy of a valid identity document, and — for a bachelor obtained at another university — a self-certification under D.P.R. 445/2000 listing the awarding university, exact title, date, final grade and every exam passed with date, grade, CFU and SSD (the SSD detail matters here, because the Art. 4 thresholds are expressed in SSD codes).

SHORT ANSWER FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: this degree is close to free. Non-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus a EUR 16 stamp; EU non-Italian citizens pay a flat EUR 200 contribution plus the regional tax and stamp. Realistic 2026/27 totals: roughly EUR 167 per year for a non-EU student and roughly EUR 367 per year for an EU non-Italian student.

THE BINDING RULES (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27, "Esoneri parziali"): "stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio... e l'imposta di bollo"; "europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR." For Italian students the standard ISEEU system applies instead: first-year students are fully EXEMPT with ISEEU up to EUR 30,000; above that a fixed component of EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component, to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those filing no ISEEU declaration; with a 50% reduction for a first-year master's student who obtained the bachelor by October of the final year of the regular course with 110 cum laude. Regional right-to-study tax bands 2026/27: EUR 130.00 (ISEEU up to 25,500), EUR 151.00 (ISEEU 25,500.01-51,000 AND students whose household resides abroad), EUR 173.00 (ISEEU above 51,000 or no ISEEU declaration); stamp duty EUR 16.00. Instalments: 1st (60% + regional tax + stamp) by 2026-11-02, 2nd (20%) by 2027-03-01, 3rd (20%) by 2027-04-30; late-enrolment surcharges of EUR 50 (to 15 Jan 2027) and EUR 110 (from 16 Jan 2027); a EUR 100 surcharge from 16 July 2027 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments.

[uncertain] THREE DIFFERENT REGIONAL-TAX FIGURES ARE PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT AND THEY DO NOT AGREE. (a) The PROGRAMME'S OWN fees page says: "EU students EUR 200/year (university fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory). Non EU students EUR 160/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)" — note it quotes EUR 140 for EU students but EUR 160 for non-EU students, an internal asymmetry that no rule justifies. (b) international.unina.it publishes a flat EUR 140/year for both. (c) The binding 2026/27 Guida gives the banded EUR 130 / 151 / 173 and expressly assigns the EUR 151 band to "studenti con nucleo familiare residente all'estero" — which is precisely the situation of most international students. USE THE GUIDA: budget EUR 151 for the regional tax. The EUR 140 and EUR 160 figures on the programme and international pages appear to be stale carry-overs from earlier years. The tuition components themselves (EUR 200 for EU, zero for non-EU) are consistent across all three sources and are not in doubt.

FUNDING: the programme's own "Fees and funding" page carries only the fee figures and no scholarship scheme of its own; regional right-to-study grants come from ADISURC, and Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs fellowships are available to applicants from eligible countries (https://studyinitaly.esteri.it/en/home_borse). Other charged services under the 2026/27 Guida include single-course enrolment (Corsi Singoli), which is the mechanism for making up missing curricular CFU.

uncertainty_notes:
1) COORDINATOR — DIRECT CONFLICT BETWEEN OFFICIAL UNINA.IT SOURCES. The central unina.it course record (https://www.unina.it/-/12930498-mathematical-engineering) and its legacy copy both list "Coordinatore: Prof.ssa Anna MERCALDO", whereas the orientation portal (updated for a.y. 2026/2027) lists "Lina Mallozzi — Degree Programme Director" and the programme's own Programme Administration page states "Coordinator: Lina Mallozzi", with Anna Mercaldo appearing there only as a member of the study-plan and review committees. The Mallozzi version is almost certainly current; the central record appears not to have been updated. Practical risk: correspondence addressed to the wrong professor. Use infomathematical-eng@unina.it or lina.mallozzi@unina.it.

2) WHICH SET OF ACADEMIC REQUIREMENTS BINDS. Three official formulations coexist and are not reconciled: (a) the closed degree-class list L-7 / L-8 / L-9 / L-23 / L-35 "or equivalent qualifications" (Art. 4, both regulation versions, and the ministerial RAD sheet); (b) the precise CFU/SSD thresholds — 24 CFU mathematics (6 MATH-02/B + 18 MATH-03/A), 12 CFU PHYS-01/A, 6 CFU INFO-01/A or IINF-05/A — which appear ONLY in the 2025/26 English Didactic Regulations and NOT in the 2023/24 Italian version; (c) the orientation portal's much softer "generally expected to hold a Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Engineering, Physics, or a closely related discipline. Each application will be assessed holistically", which names PHYSICS even though the physics class L-30 is not in the Art. 4 list; and (d) the foreign-applicant sheet, which speaks only of a "recommended background" in Mathematics or Engineering. A physics graduate is probably admissible through "titoli equipollenti" plus holistic assessment, but this is not guaranteed by any single document. Confirm with the programme before applying. Note also that NO Didactic Regulations have been published for a.y. 2026/27 — the newest is 2025/26 — although the 2026/27 STUDY PLAN has been published, so the 2025/26 admission text is the most current binding statement.

3) SSD CODE MEANINGS PARTLY INFERRED. MATH-03/A (mathematical analysis), MATH-02/B (geometry) and INFO-01/A (computer science) can be read off the programme's own 2026/2027 study plan, which tags its own courses with those codes. PHYS-01/A and IINF-05/A do not appear in the study plan, so their conventional meanings (experimental physics; information-processing systems) are inferred from standard MUR nomenclature rather than from a unina.it page.

4) THE INTERVIEW IS ANNOUNCED ONLY AS PROBABLE. "Applicants will probably contacted for an interview with Program Committee members" (the sentence is also ungrammatical in the original). No format, duration, language, syllabus or pass mark is published, and no interview is announced at all for Italian or EU applicants. Plan for an English-language academic interview but expect no published rules.

5) ENGLISH-CERTIFICATE POLICY HAS TWO WORDINGS. The Didactic Regulations say B2 is "possibly attested by suitable certification" (permissive), while the programme's annual admission rules impose a closed list of providers plus a two-year recency rule. The stricter reading is the safe one. Whether an English-medium bachelor's degree can substitute for a certificate is not addressed anywhere on unina.it for this programme.

6) EU-APPLICANT ENROLMENT DEADLINE: 31 OCTOBER vs 2 NOVEMBER 2026. Two orientation-portal pages say enrolment runs "from 16 July until 31 October 2026"; the binding University enrolment guide says the ordinary period closes 2 November 2026. 31 October 2026 falls on a Saturday, so these are probably the same deadline with and without weekend roll-over, but they are not literally identical and the programme page hedges with "usually".

7) NON-EU DEADLINE: THE PROGRAMME DELETED ITS OWN EARLIER CUT-OFF. The a.y. 25/26 admission sheet required the Universitaly application "before 31 May 2025"; the a.y. 26/27 sheet is word-for-word identical except that the date phrase has been removed entirely. So for 2026/27 only the University-wide 15 June 2026 deadline is published. Given that a programme-level date roughly two weeks earlier existed the previous year, aim for mid-May and confirm by e-mail.

8) DATE ERROR INSIDE THE OFFICIAL NON-EU BOOKLET. Its "Deadlines" page gives 31 January 2027 as the final matriculation date, but its "Matriculation" page says "31 January 2026" — impossible, since the visa deadline is 30 November 2026. 31 January 2027 is correct.

9) REGIONAL-TAX FIGURE: THREE DIFFERENT NUMBERS ON UNINA.IT. The programme's own fees page says EUR 140 for EU students but EUR 160 for non-EU students (an unexplained asymmetry); international.unina.it says a flat EUR 140 for both; the binding 2026/27 Guida gives bands of EUR 130 / 151 / 173 and expressly places students whose household resides abroad in the EUR 151 band. Budget EUR 151. The tuition components themselves (EUR 200 for EU citizens, total exemption for non-EU citizens) agree across all sources.

10) B2 ITALIAN EXEMPTION — A DRAFTING GAP IN THE UNIVERSITY TEXT. international.unina.it states the Italian B2 requirement for courses taught in Italian and expressly names "three-year degree course, magistral degree course or single-cycle magistral degree course", but the parallel exemption sentence for ENGLISH-taught courses enumerates only "three-year, five-year or single-cycle" and does not repeat "magistral degree course". The plain intent, by symmetry and by this programme's total silence on any Italian requirement, is that an English-taught two-year master's is exempt — and this programme independently attaches no Italian condition to any of its credits — but the University's own sentence does not name two-year master's degrees in the exemption.

11) VISA PROOF-OF-MEANS FIGURE NOT YEAR-LABELLED. The EUR 10,179.85/year entry-visa figure on international.unina.it carries no academic year, and the same page separately carries a EUR 6,079.45/year figure explicitly labelled "minimum required for 2022" (which relates to residence-permit renewal, not the entry visa). Treat EUR 10,179.85 as the currently published figure rather than a confirmed 2026/27-specific one.

12) NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DOCUMENT CHECKLIST is published; required_documents is assembled from the one-page admission rules plus University-level sources, so an additional item could be requested. In particular, the programme's "How to apply" page is almost empty — it only says "Get information about applying: https://www.studiare-in-italia.it/studentistranieri/ and apply to the link https://www.universitaly.it/" — so the admissions26_27.pdf, not the How to apply page, is the document to rely on.

13) COURSE CODE D71 vs D22. The programme's General Information page gives https://www.corsi.unina.it/D71/home as its institutional course site, but a "D22 MATHEMATICAL ENGINEERING" record also exists on corsi.unina.it. D22 is most likely the pre-reformulation code (the RAD sheet describes the current course as a "riformulazione" of the earlier one); this could not be confirmed because corsi.unina.it renders client-side and returned no readable content.

14) TEACHING MODE — "conventional" vs "mixed". The older ministerial RAD sheet records "Modalità di svolgimento: convenzionale", while the current Didactic Regulations record "b. Course of Studies in mixed teaching mode" and the study plan flags seven courses as "Frontal lesson/MOOC". The regulations are the more recent and more specific source.

15) SECOND-YEAR FREE-CHOICE COURSES (12 CFU, TAF D) are drawn from the University's entire catalogue subject only to consistency approval by the CCD; most of that catalogue is Italian-taught. All mandatory and curricular option courses are confirmed English, so the risk is confined to this slot.

16) 2026/27 ACADEMIC CALENDAR AND TIMETABLES NOT YET PUBLISHED on the programme site at the time of research — the newest posted are the a.y. 2025/26 calendar (teaching 15/09/2025-19/12/2025 and 02/03/2026-12/06/2026) and the a.y. 2025/26 lecture timetables. Semester dates for 2026/27 should be re-checked.

17) NON-EU SEAT CONTINGENT NOT VERIFIABLE FROM UNINA.IT — see non_eu_reserved_seats; the per-course non-EU quota for open-access degrees is published on universitaly.it, outside this task's unina.it-only source restriction.

18) THE SCHOOL-LEVEL "DISPOSITIVO" COULD NOT BE FOUND. Art. 5 says the personal-preparation check follows "the device of the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base" common to engineering master's degrees, but no such standalone document is published on scuolapsb.unina.it; that page only restates the DM 270/04 framework.

19) ACADEMIC-YEAR BASIS AND CURRENCY. All dates and amounts in this record are for A.Y. 2026/2027 and were gathered on 2026-08-30. By that date the 15 June 2026 non-EU pre-enrolment deadline had already passed and the EU enrolment window (16 July - 31 October 2026) was open. A non-EU applicant reading this must target A.Y. 2027/2028.
